name: HANS
summary: Decide whether a hypothesis follows from a premise in cases that probe three syntactic shortcuts.
overview: Heuristic Analysis for NLI Systems (HANS) tests whether models decide entailment from lexical overlap, a contiguous subsequence, or a syntactic constituent alone. Each heuristic group includes sentence pairs where the shortcut predicts the correct label and cases where it wrongly predicts entailment. [Original paper](https://aclanthology.org/P19-1334/)
methodology: The snapshot contains all 30,000 English premise–hypothesis pairs in the original evaluation file. Each of the three heuristic groups has 10,000 pairs, evenly split between entailment and non-entailment. The groups contain ten subcases each, with 1,000 examples per subcase. The prompt preserves the authors’ tokenized sentences. Keys retain the published pair IDs. The chat prompt adds a request to choose one of the two labels. The catalog date is the first dated paper release. [Pinned data instructions](https://github.com/tommccoy1/hans/blob/7299f6f657089ce06a0f98e7e81f8d0f5b7741ce/README.md) [Dated preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.01007v1)
scoring: A reply earns one point when its label matches the released answer. Following the original paper, neutral and contradiction predictions count as non-entailment. Report accuracy for each of the six heuristic-by-gold-label groups and for the 30 subcases and 60 templates in the released file. [Paper, Section 4](https://aclanthology.org/P19-1334.pdf#page=4) [Pinned official evaluator](https://github.com/tommccoy1/hans/blob/7299f6f657089ce06a0f98e7e81f8d0f5b7741ce/evaluate_heur_output.py)
limitations: The sentences come from controlled English templates designed to expose three specific shortcuts. HANS uses two labels and combines all cases where the premise fails to guarantee the hypothesis. Direct chat prompting differs from the paper’s setup, which evaluated models trained on MultiNLI. [Original paper](https://aclanthology.org/P19-1334/)
